THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    placed
        Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. Write the word none as this step's value only at the very first decision step, where the carried-in memory is blank and there are no execution steps at all. The value is plain color words separated by single spaces and nothing else: no brackets, no quotes, no commas. A carried-in none that comes with execution steps is appended to by the check below like any other value: the first appended color replaces none, so the step after the first placement writes a single word such as blue. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except after a two-part check applied in order: first, does any execution frame of this step contain an object line ending 'is held in the gripper'; second, does the scene at this decision step (the last listed frame) show the fingers about 100% open with no held line. If both hold, the oracle completed the put-into-bin subgoal: append one space and that held cube's color exactly once (if the carried-in value is none, replace it by the color). The gripper's position when the fingers opened is irrelevant (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center); fingers opening only to 67-99% in an intermediate frame are irrelevant; same-color detections that appear, shift a few px, or vanish on the table in those frames are irrelevant (detections near the opaque bin are echoes of the held cube or bin contents, not table cubes). None of these is a reason to skip the append. e.g. carried-in red becomes red red; carried-in blue blue after a held-then-released blue cube becomes blue blue blue. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. Emit the value as bare words only; any brackets, quotes or commas make it a wrong value. e.g. blue blue blue green
    arrivals
        Ordered list of [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes lying on the table, oldest-arrived first; the subgoal rule picks the first entry of the color it is working. At the very first decision step (carried-in memory blank, no execution frames): if exactly one goal-color cube is in the scene, the list is that cube. If several are, the scene does not show which came first; list first every cube of the color with the SMALLEST required count in the goal instruction (two colors needing the same count: the one the goal names first), then the next color by count; the order the goal names the colors is not the criterion. Within a color order by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first, skipping any detection within about 28 px of that center; when two cubes of one color are within about 3 px of the same distance, put the one with the larger x (the robot's left) first. Example with a goal of three blue and one green, green at [65, 109] and blue at [84, 112]: [[65, 109], [84, 112]]. A cube of a color the goal does not name is never listed. At every later step start from the carried-in list and apply, in order: (1) PICK-UP REMOVAL, only if some execution frame of this step shows the fingers about 100% open over a table cube and a later frame of this step shows them at about 46% with a cube then reported held: remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in the frame where the fingers first reached 46%. If the very first execution frame already shows a cube held (fingers 46%, a held line), this is a put-into-bin step and nothing is removed, whatever entry lies near the gripper. Never remove an entry that still matches a detection of its color within about 12 px in the last frame; never stretch the 12 px test to the nearest entry. (2) RETAIN AND REFRESH: match one-to-one with a hard cutoff: each remaining entry is matched to at most one detection of its color, the nearest within about 12 px, and a detection 13 px or more from every still-unmatched entry is new (handled in (3)). A matched entry is kept and set to that position; this match ignores the bin-echo and release-echo tests, which concern only new detections. Drop an entry with no such detection. (3) APPEND NEW: a goal-color table detection in the last frame that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended unless it is a bin echo or a release echo. A detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center is a bin echo only if it was present in the scene at the first decision step, or its color already appears in the carried `placed`, or this step released a cube of that color; a detection of a color not in `placed` that first appears in some execution frame of this step and is still at the same place (within about 12 px) in the last frame is a genuine new cube however near the bin it is: append it, in the order of the frame where it first appeared. The release frame is the first execution frame of this step where the fingers are about 100% open with no held line; a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it. A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported in that frame, or that has moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame; it is excluded even when far from the bin center. A detection that was already at its place in the first execution frame of the step, or that matches a carried entry, is never an echo. A detection that appears mid-step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and stays put is a genuine new cube: append it. In a step that ends with a cube held (a pick-up step: first execution frame shows no held line, last frame shows one) there is no release frame, so the release-echo and moved-with-the-gripper tests do not apply; a new goal-color detection that appears near the gripper or near the just-grasped cube during such a step and is in the last frame is appended like any other, excluding only bin echoes. (4) When several new detections are appended, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared, earliest first, tracking each across frames within about 12 px; same-frame arrivals follow that frame's listing order. Order is otherwise never changed. Example: carried [[77, 139]], a pick-up step closing on [77, 139], with a red cube that appeared at [100, 66] several frames earlier far from bin and gripper, and two red detections within 28 px of the bin: write [[100, 66]]. Write the list as nested brackets exactly like the example. e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory fields `placed` and `arrivals` as updated at this step. `placed` is space-separated color words (the word none when nothing has been placed); a color's count is the number of times its word appears, and none counts as zero for every color. Rule 1 (holding): The scene at this decision step is the LAST listed observed step; check that frame first, before any earlier execution frame. If any object line in that last frame ends in 'is held in the gripper', or the fingers there are partly closed (about 46% or less open), choose B: put it into the bin, before any other rule is considered. This holds whatever `placed` contains and however many cubes lie on the table. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. `placed` here is the value as updated at this step: a step whose execution frames show a cube held and whose last frame shows the fingers about 100% open with nothing held counts that cube as placed, so choose C when every goal count is then met, even if cubes of the goal colors remain on the table, including one that reappeared near the bin after the release. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Color choice: a color whose count in the updated `placed` meets its requirement is finished and is never picked again, even if cubes of that color remain visible on the table. If the last word of `placed` is a color that is still short, pick that color again (one color is finished before the other is started). Otherwise, including when `placed` is none, the working color is the color of the first entry of `arrivals` whose color is still short (the oldest cube of a needed color on the table). At the first decision step, where several goal-color cubes may be present with no arrival order to read, the working color is the color with the SMALLEST required count in the goal instruction (equal counts: the one the goal names first); `arrivals` as written at this step begins with that color, nearest the bin first, so that is where the first pick goes. At every later step the goal's counts and naming order play no part in the choice of color. Point at that cube's center as shown in the scene at this decision step. A candidate is a cube of the working color reported as a table cube (not held) in the scene at this decision step. New cubes genuinely appear on the table during the episode, so a detection that was absent from earlier frames is still a candidate, and one that wobbles a few px between frames while the arm passes near it is still a candidate. Excluded, at every step including step #1: a bin echo, meaning a detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center that was there at step #1, or whose color already appears in `placed`, or whose color was released in this step (a cube 30 px or more from the center that stays in place is real, and a cube of a not-yet-placed color that appeared mid-step and stayed put is a candidate wherever it lies); a release echo, meaning a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame (the first execution frame of this step with the fingers about 100% open and no held line) within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame, excluded however far it is from the bin; a detection already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step, or matching a carried `arrivals` entry within about 12 px, is not an echo; and a detection whose position tracks the gripper from frame to frame. Among several candidates, choose the one that comes first in `arrivals` (match entries to last-frame detections within about 12 px): the oracle picks the cube of the working color that has been on the table longest. Only when the candidates cannot be told apart by `arrivals` (none of them matches an entry) fall back to the one nearest the bin's reported center that is not excluded above. The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame; a point within about 3 px of that center is correct. Cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is none, so pick up the cube that is first in `arrivals` among those of a needed color: with one goal-color cube in the scene, that cube; with several, the cube of the color with the smallest required count in the goal (equal counts: the color named first) that is nearest the bin's reported center while at least about 28 px from it; when two such cubes are within about 3 px of the same distance to the bin, the one with the larger x (the robot's left). If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the first `arrivals` entry of a needed color, else the cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not within 28 px of it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not within 28 px of the bin. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

ButtonUnmask.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    picks_done
        Number of container pick-ups completed so far, always written as a number, never left blank. If no value was carried in (as at the first decision step), treat the carried-in value as 0. Then look only at the scene at this decision step, meaning the last frame shown, and ignore every earlier execution frame (in particular a frame at the start of the execution that still shows a container held from before). If that last frame shows a container held in the gripper, write that number + 1; otherwise, including when the gripper is empty and open with every container resting on the table, write that number unchanged. It does not change when the container is put down. At the first decision step this is 0. e.g. 0 at the first decision step, 1 at the step where the first container hangs in the gripper, still 1 at the step after it has been set down
    target_cube_positions
        If the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown) shows loose cubes and no containers anywhere (the scene before the button is pressed), read the goal instruction, list the cubes it names in the order it names them, and write the [y, x] of each of those cubes as an ordered list in that same order; leave out any cube the goal does not name. Otherwise copy the carried-in list unchanged, never editing it from a cube briefly exposed under a lifted container. e.g. goal naming blue then red: [[78, 157], [106, 105]]; goal naming only red: [[73, 93]]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Every condition in Rules 1-3 is evaluated on the scene at the decision step only, meaning the last frame shown. The four outcomes, in order: empty carried-in memory and no execution frames -> 0; carried 0 and a press in this step's frames -> 1; carried 1 and a press in this step's frames -> 2; carried 2, or any container held or grasped in this step -> 2. A frame saying a button 'is pressed down' in this step is a press of this step even if that button is the one the robot was already heading for. In detail: write 0 at the first step (empty carried-in memory, no execution frames). Otherwise write the carried-in count plus 1 if any execution frame of this step says a button 'is pressed down' OR shows the gripper within about 6 px of a button's [y, x] at height below about 0.06 with fingers closed; otherwise the carried-in count. A frame with the gripper over a container (height around 0.1, 20 px or more from the nearest button) is not a press, even if a button is missing from the list in that frame because it is occluded. Each step shows at most one press, so the count never rises by more than 1. If any frame of this step shows a container 'held in the gripper' or the gripper lowered onto a container with fingers closing, write 2 regardless of the carried count, because both presses precede any pick-up. e.g. 2

fields.name: green_container
fields.description: [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. At the first step (empty carried-in memory, no execution frames) write the green cube's own [y, x] from the scene, and likewise red_container and blue_container with their cubes, buttons_pressed=0 and picked_colors=[]; no field is left blank at the first step. SECOND, before any chaining, for this field and likewise for red_container and blue_container: if green is already in the carried-in picked_colors, or any frame of this step shows the green cube itself (its container lifted or 'held in the gripper'), do not chain containers for green; write the cube's position from the last frame in which the cube is visible, and keep that position at every later step even when a container is set down over it and only containers are listed in the last frames. Never write the position of a container 'held in the gripper' or of a container lowered back onto the cube. Only for colors not yet exposed, apply what follows. At every step whose frames show containers, rewrite this field, and likewise red_container and blue_container, whether or not the color is named in the goal and whether or not its container moved. When containers first appear, take the container standing on the carried-in position. At every later step: (1) if the carried value is a cube position (first step with containers), take the container standing on it in the first frame shown; (2) otherwise take the container in the FIRST frame shown nearest the carried value, even if it is 10-15 px away because the glide was already under way; (3) step frame to frame, each time picking the container with the smallest displacement from the one just chosen; (4) write that container's last-frame position. Never match the carried value straight to the last frame. Scale: frames are sparse, about 16 ticks apart, so a gliding container is normally 15-35 px from its previous-frame position; 'smallest displacement' is judged at that scale, and 'a few pixels' means only a container that did not move. Mandatory joint procedure: (a) MOVED-STEP TRIGGER: if any frame of this step lists a container more than about 6 px from every container of the previous frame (the previous step's last frame counts as the frame before the first), this is a moved step and you MUST run the chain for ALL THREE colors through every frame as a ONE-TO-ONE ASSIGNMENT: in each frame each container is assigned to exactly one color, so two fields can never end on the same container, and a container that one color leaves must be taken up by another color; (b) when the nearest candidate for one color is a near-tie (displacements within a few pixels of each other), choose the assignment that also gives the other colors a distinct nearest container with the smallest total displacement; (c) an identical container layout in the first and last frames of a step does not mean nothing moved; if middle frames show displacement, the result is usually a swap of two colors, and the chain decides which; This holds without exception, including when the first frame already shows containers 10-15 px off the carried values and when the last frame shows containers exactly on the carried values. Per frame transition choose the one-to-one assignment with the smallest total displacement (e.g. 23+29 beats 28+29). (d) consistency check before writing: the three written values must be three different containers of the last frame, and if one field moved to a new container, the field that carried that container's old position must have moved too. Joint example: carried green [100, 166] and blue [130, 162]; frames show one container gliding [101, 168], [110, 178], [125, 182], [130, 163], [130, 160] while the other glides [130, 162], [121, 151], [106, 147], [102, 165], [101, 168]; write green_container=[130, 160] and blue_container=[101, 168], even if the goal names only one of them. Worked example of the swap trap: carried [131, 115]; first frame has containers at [118, 118] and [113, 162], pick [118, 118]; next frame it is at [99, 134], next at [101, 161]; write [101, 161], although the OTHER container, which came from [113, 162], now stands at [131, 116], almost exactly the carried value. SWAP TRAP rule: in a moved step a last-frame container standing within 5 px of the carried value is NOT a match; matching a carried value straight to a last-frame container is forbidden, and the only legal path is carried value -> nearest first-frame container -> frame by frame -> last frame. Unmoved step: every frame's containers stand within about 6 px of the previous frame's; then write the same container's last-frame position. Containers gliding around each other usually finish swapped, but trust the chain, not the assumption (one circling pass swaps them, two passes return them). Sanity check after a moved step: two containers that circled around each other while the third stood still almost always end swapped; if the chain says nothing swapped, recompute the chain before writing. Write the followed container's position in the last frame. If any frame shows the green cube itself (container lifted or 'held in the gripper'), write the cube's position in the last frame it is visible, and keep that cube position at later steps even once a container is lowered back over it. e.g. [109, 126]

fields.name: red_container
fields.description: [y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly as green_container: first, if red is in the carried-in picked_colors or the red cube is visible in any frame of this step, write the cube's last visible position and ignore every container, including the held one and the one lowered back onto the cube, at this and every later step; otherwise, rewritten at every step that shows containers even when red is not named in the goal and even when its container stood still (snapping from the cube's original position to the container on it): write the red cube's position at the first step; take the container that covers it; chain smallest-displacement matches from the first frame shown to the last (trust the chain, not an assumed swap; a last-frame container coinciding with the carried position is the swap trap, not a match; frames are sparse so 15-35 px per-frame glides are normal and 'a few pixels' means a container that did not move; whenever any frame lists a container more than about 6 px from every container of the previous frame the step is a moved step and the joint chain MUST be run and written, even if the last frame shows containers exactly on the carried values; after a moved step, if the chain says the two circling containers did not swap, recompute before writing), chained jointly with green and blue as a one-to-one assignment per frame, near-ties broken by consistency with the other chains, re-chained whenever any frame shows a container displaced even if the step's first and last layouts look identical, the three written values being three distinct last-frame containers. Example: carried red [112, 194] passes [121, 184], [119, 162] (chosen over [95, 182] because blue's chain takes that one), [103, 153], last frame [101, 152]; write [101, 152]; e.g. [101, 165]

fields.name: blue_container
fields.description: [y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly as green_container: first, if blue is in the carried-in picked_colors or the blue cube is visible in any frame of this step, write the cube's last visible position and ignore every container, including the held one and the one lowered back onto the cube, at this and every later step; otherwise, rewritten at every step that shows containers even when blue is not named in the goal and even when its container stood still (snapping from the cube's original position to the container on it): write the blue cube's position at the first step; take the container that covers it; chain smallest-displacement matches from the first frame shown to the last (trust the chain, not an assumed swap; never match the carried value straight to a last-frame container, even one standing within a pixel or two of it; frames are sparse so 15-35 px per-frame glides are normal and 'a few pixels' means a container that did not move; whenever any frame lists a container more than about 6 px from every container of the previous frame the step is a moved step and the joint chain MUST be run and written, even if the last frame shows containers exactly on the carried values; after a moved step, if the chain says the two circling containers did not swap, recompute before writing), chained jointly with green and red as a one-to-one assignment per frame, near-ties broken by consistency with the other chains, re-chained whenever any frame shows a container displaced even if the step's first and last layouts look identical, the three written values being three distinct last-frame containers. Example: carried blue [101, 152] passes [95, 163], [95, 182], [112, 194], last frame [114, 195]; write [114, 195]; e.g. [102, 79]

fields.name: picked_colors
fields.description: Written as the exact JSON text, double quotes, no spaces: [] at the first step and whenever empty, ["red"] after the red cube is exposed, ["red","green"] after both; a single-quoted list such as ['red'] is a mismatch. Carried-in list; append the color of a cube that appears visible beneath a lifted or 'held in the gripper' container among this step's frames, if that color is not already in the list. e.g. ["green"]

    grasp_point
        At the first decision step (demonstration shown, memory empty): find the demonstration frame where the gripper is at its lowest height (about 0.01-0.03) and the fingers have first dropped from 100% open toward closed (about 22% open, or a frame at about 50% while still closing); pick the peg head or peg tail entry whose coordinates are nearest the gripper in that frame; then write that same end's coordinates as they appear in the start-of-execution scene (pegs are at their demonstration t=0 positions). At every later step copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. [114, 212]

        At the first decision step: head if the nearest entry to the gripper at the demonstration grasp frame (lowest height, fingers first dropped from 100% open toward closed, ~22% or ~50% while closing) is a peg head, tail if it is a peg tail.     insert_side
        At the first decision step: look at the last few demonstration frames, where the gripper is low (height about 0.04), fingers still closed, and gripper y close to the aperture box y. Write grasp_point, grasp_end and insert_side at this step (grasp_point is this same point). 2. If the scene shows a peg end 'is held in the gripper' (fingers about 22% open, gripper raised): the pick is done. If insert_side is right, choose B, insert the peg from the right side. If insert_side is left, choose C, insert the peg from the left side. 3. If the scene shows no peg held and the memory already holds grasp_point (the pick failed or dropped): choose A again and point at grasp_point, using the current position of the peg end of class grasp_end nearest that stored point. 4. Carry all memory fields forward unchanged.

MoveCube.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    method
        The way the demonstration moved the cube. At the first decision step, read it from the demonstration steps: `pick` if the cube is marked as held in the gripper while the gripper is well above the table (height above about 0.08) with fingers partly closed (about 40-60% open) and the cube is then released over the target; `hook` if the stick (peg) is marked as held in the gripper with fingers closed to about 20-25% and is dragged against the cube toward the target; `push` if the fingers close to about 0% at table height (height below about 0.04) and the cube slides to the target without ever being lifted or any stick being held. At every later step copy the value carried in unchanged; never write `unknown` after the first step. e.g. hook

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    The menu options need no target point; if a point is demanded anyway, point at the object the option names (the cube for C, D, E; the stick for A; the target for B and E would be the cube's destination, but prefer the cube). An episode starts at the first decision step with empty memory; first fill `method` from the demonstration steps, then choose by it. Rules, applied in whatever situation the policy stands in: - If `method` is `push`: choose C (close gripper and push the cube to the target). This is the only subgoal for a push episode. In every rule below, what is in hand is read from the gripper in the scene at this decision step alone, never from memory: raised above about 0.10 with fingers at about 20-30% is the peg in hand, raised with fingers at about 40-60% is the cube in hand, fingers 100% open or about 0% is nothing in hand; the stick's or cube's listed coordinates staying unchanged and the absence of a held mark do not count against a grasp. - If `method` is `pick` and nothing is in hand: choose D (pick up the cube). - If `method` is `pick` and the cube is in hand: choose E (place the cube onto the target). - If `method` is `hook` and nothing is in hand: choose A (pick up the peg). - If `method` is `hook` and the peg is in hand: choose B (hook the cube to the target with the peg). If a situation has no rule: if `method` cannot be told, decide by what the scene shows - fingers partly closed with the cube raised means E, fingers closed to about 20-25% with the stick raised means B; otherwise if the demonstration showed the stick held choose A, if it showed the cube lifted choose D, and if neither choose C. Never choose E without the cube in hand and never choose B without the peg in hand, 'in hand' being judged by the finger opening and gripper height at this decision step as defined above, not by object coordinates.

PatternLock.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    plan
        The ordered list of menu letters the demonstration traces. If this step shows DEMONSTRATION STEPS (the first step, memory empty), build it now and never change it afterwards: the highlighted target at demo t=0 is the start (this start marker may be labelled 'highlighted area' rather than 'highlighted target'; use its coordinates as the starting highlighted position for the first dy/dx computation); each time a different target becomes highlighted in the demo frames, take dy = new y minus previous highlighted y and dx = new x minus previous highlighted x (coordinates at the frame it first appears). |dy| >= 8 with dy > 0 means forward, dy < 0 means backward; |dx| >= 8 with dx > 0 means left, dx < 0 means right; both over threshold means the diagonal (forward=A, backward=B, left=C, right=D, forward-left=E, forward-right=F, backward-left=G, backward-right=H). One letter per newly highlighted target, in demo order. If the step shows no demonstration, copy the carried-in plan character for character. Write the value as one plain string of bare capital letters in order, with nothing else: no quotes of any kind, no brackets, no commas, no spaces. Position 0 is the first move. The value is compared character by character, so EDGH is right and ["E", "D", "G", "H"] or ['E', 'D', 'G', 'H'] are both wrong. e.g. EDGH
    moves_done
        How many planned moves have been finished by the scene at this step. Write 0 when the step shows demonstration steps and the carried memory is empty (first step). Otherwise the step shows execution steps of one completed move, so write the carried-in moves_done plus one. e.g. 2

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Every episode starts at the first decision step with empty memory and the demonstration shown; the subgoal there is the first character of the plan string just built from the demonstration (position 0). At every decision step, the subgoal is the character at position moves_done (0-based) of the plan string, where moves_done is the value written at THIS step: 0 at the first step, carried value plus one at later steps). So the first step performs plan[0], the second step plan[1], and so on. No subgoal needs a point. After a move finishes, the next decision step always advances to the next plan letter regardless of where the gripper ended; never repeat or skip. If moves_done is at or beyond the length of the plan (nothing remains), repeat the last character of the plan string. If the plan could not be built (no demonstration visible and empty plan), derive the direction from the two highlighted targets currently visible if there are two (direction from the older-looking one near the gripper to the other, same dy/dx rule), otherwise choose A: move forward. In any other unforeseen situation, pick plan[moves_done] if it exists, else A.

PickHighlight.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    button_pressed
        Write `no` when the memory carried in says `no` (or is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the press (neither the pressed-down label nor the gripper at the button's position at low height with closed fingers). At the first decision step, when the memory carried in is empty, write the starting value `no` explicitly; never leave the field blank. Write `yes` as soon as any execution step shown at this step either says the button is pressed down, or shows the gripper within a few pixels of the button's [y, x] at a height of about 0.02-0.04 with fingers nearly closed (0-2% open); the highlighted areas then vanish from the listing before the decision step, which confirms the press.     demo_moves
        If the memory carried in is empty (first decision step), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS and write one menu letter per leg, in order. First fix the target slots from the first demonstration frame (the highlighted target plus every listed target; slots are spaced roughly 30 px or more apart in x). Then walk through the demonstration frames and, at every frame, assign the highlighted target to the nearest slot; every frame where the highlighted target is assigned to a different slot than in the previous frame ends one leg and starts the next, so the number of letters is exactly the number of such slot changes. A slot change always shows as a jump of tens of pixels to where a previously non-highlighted target sat. If the highlighted position is within a few pixels (under about 10 px) of the previous frame's highlighted position, it is the same target with coordinate jitter and nothing has changed; do not count it. Count a change even when the gripper returns to a target it already visited, even when the leg lasts only a few frames, and even when the change appears only in the very last demonstration frame; a visited target means a visited slot. A frame with two targets highlighted at once is the change frame: the newly highlighted target is the new one. For each leg: new target x smaller than the previous target x means RIGHT, larger means LEFT. The leg's frames are the frames AFTER its opening frame and BEFORE its closing change frame whose single highlighted target is the leg's starting target. For the first leg the opening frame is the very first demonstration frame, so its frames are the second frame onward until the first change. Never use frames at or after the closing change frame; those belong to the next leg and are often on the opposite side of the stick. The reference stick is the one cube whose x lies between the x of the starting target and the x of the new target. In each of the leg's frames compare gripper y with that cube's y in the same frame (the cube may shift slightly when brushed): gripper y smaller than the cube's y means it passed the BACKWARD side, larger means FORWARD. Do not compare the gripper with the new target's y and do not let the gripper's movement in the following leg decide the side. LEFT+backward=A, RIGHT+forward=B, LEFT+forward=C, RIGHT+backward=D. At every later step copy the list carried in unchanged. Write the list single-quoted with comma and space between letters, never with double quotes. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']
    legs_done

    crossings
        Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the carried-in cube_side (skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x, where cube_x and target_x are the SECOND numbers of the cube's and the target's [y, x] positions) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2
    cube_side
        The side of the target line the cube is on in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step): 'smaller_x' if cube_x < target_x, 'larger_x' if cube_x > target_x. cube_x is the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position and target_x the SECOND number of the target's [y, x] position; the first numbers are y and are never used here. Worked example: cube at [131, 61] and target at [107, 145] -> compare 61 with 145 -> 61 < 145 -> smaller_x. Overwrite it every step; at the first step read it from the single frame shown. e.g. smaller_x
    peak_speed
        Take the carried-in peak_speed (0 if memory is empty). Build the frame list: first the carried-in position (last_cube_x at time last_t) if memory is not empty, then every frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. cube_x is always the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position. For every consecutive pair in that list write the x change |cube_x(later) - cube_x(earlier)| and the timestep gap; if the gap is at least 8, write the quotient rounded to one decimal with halves rounding up (3.875 -> 3.9); if the gap is below 8 timesteps (common just before the decision scene, where detection wobble dominates), skip that pair. Write the largest of the carried-in value and all the counted quotients. It never decreases. At the first step (empty memory, one frame) write 0. e.g. 2.0
    last_cube_x
        Write the cube's x-coordinate in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step), as a plain number. x is the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position: a cube at [85, 52] gives 52. Overwrite it every step; at the first step read it from the single frame shown. It is read at the next step as the earlier member of the pair with the first frame shown there, both for peak_speed and, when that step shows a single frame, for judging the cube's motion. e.g. 52

Where the two configurations are identical write 'no swap'. Where they differ, exactly two spots changed occupants: write 'swap k: spot X <-> spot Y; L now = ...'
